note: hand-written by node GA2 before any GA2 extractor change ran, by reading the Go (the fixture is read, not run). Each case is a module under this directory. An rpc entry is a state string or an object of the facts compared exactly (state, codes, unread = a grpc_code_not_literal item). Codes are every code of the rpc but unimplemented stubs, whatever their kind.

ctormap.why: SG-1/SG-2: the code is looked up in a string-keyed package map by a constructor, `st, ok := m[code]; if !ok { st = codes.Unknown }`, through one, two and three constructor levels; a key the map lacks is the fallback; a key not constant is unread; a local with a multi-value assignment is never single-valued (Two: unread, never the fallback alone)

passthru.why: SG-3/HO5-3/HO5-4: an error parameter takes, at each call, the errors of the argument; `return err` under errors.As / status.FromError passes on only status errors (a plain error cannot satisfy it); `x.GRPCStatus().Err()` on the errors.As target is the parameter's status codes; an errors.Is switch is entered only on the branches of the sentinels passed

icodes.why: SG-3 (interceptor codes of interceptors that are not literal auth gates): each interceptor's codes reach the rpcs whose method passes its literal method tests (prefix, equality, a literal map); a code under a method test that is not literal, or from a module function the method name decides, reaches no rpc; the handler's own answer is not the interceptor's

desctable.why: HO5-1: `RegisterService(b.desc, b.impl)` over a range of a slice literal, returned by a module function or written in the loop, registers each row's descriptor and implementation
